speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You present with a generalized nonpruritic rash and a recent history of high fever and seizure. To determine the underlying cause, can you tell me your age and how many days have passed since the onset of your fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Scarlet Fever (Streptococcus pyogenes infection). The presentation of high fever, seizure, and a generalized nonpruritic rash starting on the trunk in an infant with up-to-date immunizations is highly suggestive of a bacterial etiology like scarlet fever rather than viral exanthems or Kawasaki disease. I will request a throat culture and Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential to confirm the presence of streptococcus and assess for bacterial load. REQUEST TEST: Throat_Culture, CBC_with_differential.
